entries.b6a5e7c7df67619a6d683c9da75b9dc25e423da4: <div sID="gen25049" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="16" osisID="Mark.16" sID="Mark.16"/> <div eID="gen25049" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25050" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen25051" type="x-p"/> In this chapter, we have a short account of the resurrection and ascension of the Lord Jesus: and the joys and triumphs which it furnished all believers with, will be very acceptable to those who sympathised and suffered with Christ in the foregoing chapters. Here is, I. Christ's resurrection notified by an angel to the women that came to the sepulchre to anoint him, <reference osisRef="Mark.16.1-Mark.16.8">ver. 1-8</reference>. II. His appearance to Mary Magdalene, and the account she gave of it to the disciples, <reference osisRef="Mark.16.9-Mark.16.11">ver. 9-11</reference>. III. His appearance to the two disciples, going to Emmaus, and the report they made of it to their brethren, <reference osisRef="Mark.16.12-Mark.16.13">ver. 12, 13</reference>. IV. His appearance to the eleven with the commission he gave them to set up his kingdom in the world, and full instructions and credentials in order thereunto,, <reference osisRef="Mark.16.14-Mark.16.18">ver. 14-18</reference>. V. His ascension into heaven, the apostles' close application to their work, and God's owning of them in it, <reference osisRef="Mark.16.19-Mark.16.20">ver. 19, 20</reference>.
entries.7c0d2bb64ca577d1470f9984cfeeb58fc06a8eb1: <div eID="gen25051" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen25050" type="introduction"/> <title type="x-s3">The Women at the Sepulchre; The Apostles Reproved.</title> <div sID="gen25052" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">1</hi> And when the sabbath was past, Mary Magdalene, and Mary the <hi type="italic">mother</hi> of James, and Salome, had bought sweet spices, that they might come and anoint him. <hi type="super">2</hi> And very early in the morning the first <hi type="italic">day</hi> of the week, they came unto the sepulchre at the rising of the sun. <hi type="super">3</hi> And they said among themselves, Who shall roll us away the stone from the door of the sepulchre? <hi type="super">4</hi> And when they looked, they saw that the stone was rolled away: for it was very great. <hi type="super">5</hi> And entering into the sepulchre, they saw a young man sitting on the right side, clothed in a long white garment; and they were affrighted. <hi type="super">6</hi> And he saith unto them, Be not affrighted: Ye seek Jesus of Nazareth, which was crucified: he is risen; he is not here: behold the place where they laid him. <hi type="super">7</hi> But go your way, tell his disciples and Peter that he goeth before you into Galilee: there shall ye see him, as he said unto you. <hi type="super">8</hi> And they went out quickly, and fled from the sepulchre; for they trembled and were amazed: neither said they any thing to any <hi type="italic">man;</hi> for they were afraid. <div eID="gen25052" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25053" type="x-p"/> Never was there such a <hi type="italic">sabbath</hi> since the sabbath was first instituted as this was, which the first words of this chapter tell us was <hi type="italic">now past;</hi> during all this sabbath our Lord Jesus lay in the grave. It was <hi type="italic">to him</hi> a sabbath of <hi type="italic">rest,</hi> but a <hi type="italic">silent</hi> sabbath, it was to his disciples a melancholy sabbath, spent in tears and fears. Never were the sabbath services in the temple such an <hi type="italic">abomination to God,</hi> though they had been often so, as they were now, when the chief priests, who presided in them, had their hands full of blood, the blood of Christ. Well, this sabbath is over, and the first day of the week is the first day of a new world. We have here, <div eID="gen25053" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25054" type="x-p"/> I. The affectionate visit which the good women that had attended Christ, now made it to his sepulchre—not a <hi type="italic">superstitious</hi> one, but a <hi type="italic">pious</hi> one. They set out from their lodgings <hi type="italic">very early in the morning,</hi> at break of day, or sooner; but either they had a long walk, or they met with some hindrance, so that it was <hi type="italic">sun-rising</hi> by the time they got to the sepulchre. The had <hi type="italic">bought sweet spices</hi> too, and came not only to <hi type="italic">bedew</hi> the dead body with their tears (for nothing could more renew their grief than this), but to <hi type="italic">perfume</hi> it with their <hi type="italic">spices,</hi> <reference osisRef="Mark.16.1">v. 1</reference>. Nicodemus had bought a very large quantity of <hi type="italic">dry spices, myrrh</hi> and <hi type="italic">aloes,</hi> which served to dry the wounds, and dry up the blood, <reference osisRef="John.19.39">John xix. 39</reference>. But these good women did not think that enough; they bought spices, perhaps of another kind, some perfumed oils, to <hi type="italic">anoint him.</hi> Note, The respect which others have showed to Christ's name, should not hinder us from showing our respect to it. <div eID="gen25054" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25055" type="x-p"/> II. The care they were in about the rolling away of the stone, and the superseding of that care (<reference osisRef="Mark.16.3-Mark.16.4">v. 3, 4</reference>); <hi type="italic">They said among themselves,</hi> as they were coming along, and now drew near the sepulchre, <hi type="italic">Who shall roll us away the stone from the door of the sepulchre? For it was very great,</hi> more than they with their united strength could move. They should have thought of this before they came out, and then discretion would have bid them not go, unless they had those to go with them, who could do it. And there was another difficulty much greater than this, to be got over, which they knew nothing of, to wit, a guard of soldiers set to <hi type="italic">keep</hi> the sepulchre; who, had they come before they were frightened away, would have frightened them away. But their gracious love to Christ carried them to the sepulchre; and see how by the time they came thither, both these difficulties were removed, both the <hi type="italic">stone</hi> which they <hi type="italic">knew of,</hi> and the <hi type="italic">guard</hi> which they <hi type="italic">knew not of.</hi> They <hi type="italic">saw that the stone was rolled away,</hi> which was the first thing that amazed them. Note, They who are carried by a holy zeal, to seek Christ diligently, will find the difficulties that lie in their way strangely to vanish, and themselves helped over them beyond their expectation. <div eID="gen25055" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25056" type="x-p"/> III. The assurance that was given them by an angel, that the Lord Jesus was risen from the dead, and had taken leave of his sepulchre, and had left him there to tell those so who came thither to enquire after him. <div eID="gen25056" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25057" type="x-p"/> 1. They <hi type="italic">entered into the sepulchre,</hi> at least, a little way in, and saw that the body of Jesus was not there where they had left it the other night. He, who by his death undertook to pay our debt, in his resurrection took out our acquittance, for it was a fair and legal discharge, by which it appealed that his satisfaction was accepted for all the purposes for which it was intended, and the matter in dispute was determined by an incontestable evidence that he was the Son of God. <div eID="gen25057" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25058" type="x-p"/> 2. They saw a <hi type="italic">young man sitting on the right side</hi> of the sepulchre. The angel appeared in the likeness of <hi type="italic">a man,</hi> of a <hi type="italic">young man;</hi> for angels, though created in the beginning, grow not <hi type="italic">old,</hi> but are always the same perfection of beauty and strength; and so shall glorified saints be, when they are <hi type="italic">as the angels.</hi> This angel was <hi type="italic">sitting</hi> on <hi type="italic">the right hand</hi> as they went into the sepulchre, <hi type="italic">clothed with a long white garment,</hi> a garment down to the feet, such as great men were arrayed with. The sight of him might justly have encouraged them, but they were <hi type="italic">affrighted.</hi> Thus many times that which should be matter of comfort to us, through our own mistakes and misapprehensions proves a terror to us. <div eID="gen25058" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25059" type="x-p"/> 3. He silences their fears by assuring them that here was cause enough for triumph, but none for trembling (<reference osisRef="Mark.16.6">v. 6</reference>); <hi type="italic">He saith to them, Be not affrighted.</hi> Note, As angels rejoice in the conversation of sinners, so they do also in the consolation of sinners. Be not affrighted, for, (1.) "Ye are faithful lovers of Jesus Christ, and therefore, instead of being <hi type="italic">confounded,</hi> out to be <hi type="italic">comforted. Ye seek Jesus of Nazareth, which was crucified.</hi>" Note, The enquiries of believing souls after Christ, have a particular regard to him as <hi type="italic">crucified</hi> (<reference osisRef="1Cor.2.2">1 Cor. ii. 2</reference>), that they may know him, and the fellowship of his sufferings. His being <hi type="italic">lifted up from the earth,</hi> is that which <hi type="italic">draws all men unto him.</hi> Christ's cross is the ensign to which the Gentiles seek. Observe, He speaks of Jesus as one that <hi type="italic">was crucified;</hi> "The thing is <hi type="italic">past,</hi> that scene is over, ye must not dwell so much upon the sad circumstances of his crucifixion as to be unapt to believe the joyful news of his resurrection. He was <hi type="italic">crucified in weakness,</hi> yet that doth not hinder but that he may be raised in power, and therefore ye that seek him, be not <hi type="italic">afraid of missing</hi> of him." He <hi type="italic">was</hi> crucified, but he <hi type="italic">is</hi> glorified; and the shame of his sufferings is so far from lessening the glory of his exaltation, that that glory perfectly wipes away all the reproach of his sufferings. And therefore after his entrance upon his glory, he never drew any veil over his sufferings, nor was shy of having his cross spoken of. The angel here that proclaims his resurrection, calls him Jesus that <hi type="italic">was crucified.</hi> He himself owns (<reference osisRef="Rev.1.18">Rev. i. 18</reference>), <hi type="italic">I am he that liveth, and was dead;</hi> and he appears in the midst of the praises of the heavenly host as a <hi type="italic">Lamb that had been slain,</hi> <reference osisRef="Rev.5.6">Rev. v. 6</reference>. (2.) "It will therefore be good news to you, to hear that, instead of anointing him dead, you may rejoice in him living. <hi type="italic">He is risen, he is not here,</hi> not dead, but alive again. We cannot as yet show you <hi type="italic">him,</hi> but hereafter you will see him, and you may here see <hi type="italic">the place where they laid him.</hi> You see he is gone hence, not stolen either by his enemies or by his friends, but <hi type="italic">risen.</hi>" <div eID="gen25059" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25060" type="x-p"/> 4. He orders them to give speedy notice of this to his disciples. Thus they were made the apostles of the apostles, which was a recompence of their affection and fidelity to him, in attending him on the cross, to the grave, and in the grave. They first came, and were first served; no other of the disciples durst come near his sepulchre, or enquire after him; so little danger was there of their coming by night to <hi type="italic">steal him away,</hi> that none came near him but a few women, who were not able so much as to <hi type="italic">roll away the stone.</hi> <div eID="gen25060" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25061" type="x-p"/> (1.) They must tell the <hi type="italic">disciples,</hi> that <hi type="italic">he is risen.</hi> It is a dismal time with them, their dear Master is dead, and all their hopes and joys are buried in his grave; they look upon their cause as sunk, and themselves ready to fall an easy prey into the hands of their enemies, so that there remains no more spirit in them, they are perfectly at their wits' end, and every one is contriving how to shift for himself. "O, go quickly to them," said the angel, "tell them that <hi type="italic">their Master is risen;</hi> this will put some life and spirit into them, and keep them from sinking into despair." Note, [1.] Christ is not ashamed to own his poor disciples, no, not now that he is in his exalted state; his preferment doth not make him shy of them, for he took early care to have it <hi type="italic">notified</hi> to them. [2.] Christ is not extreme to mark what <hi type="italic">they</hi> do amiss, whose hearts are upright with him. The disciples had very unkindly deserted him, and yet he testified this concern for them. [3.] Seasonable comforts shall be sent to those that are lamenting after the Lord Jesus, and he will find a time to manifest himself to them. <div eID="gen25061" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25062" type="x-p"/> (2.) They must be sure to tell Peter. This is particularly taken notice of by this evangelist, who is supposed to have written by Peter's direction. If it were told the disciples, it would be told Peter, for, as a token of his repentance for disowning his Master, he still associated with his disciples; yet he is particularly named: <hi type="italic">Tell Peter,</hi> for, [1.] It will be good news to him, more welcome to him than to any of them; for he is in sorrow for sin, and no tidings can be more welcome to true penitents than to hear of the resurrection of Christ, because he rose again for <hi type="italic">their justification.</hi> [2.] He will be afraid, lest the joy of this good news do not belong to him. Had the angel said only, <hi type="italic">Go, tell his disciples,</hi> poor Peter would have been ready to sigh, and say, "But I doubt I cannot look upon myself as one of them, for I disowned him, and deserve to be disowned by him;" to obviate that, "Go to Peter by name, and tell him, he shall be as welcome as any of the rest to <hi type="italic">see</hi> him in Galilee." Note, A sight of Christ will be very welcome to a true penitent, and a true penitent shall be very welcome to a sight of Christ, for there is joy in heaven concerning him. <div eID="gen25062" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25063" type="x-p"/> (3.) They must appoint them all, and Peter by name, to give him the meeting in Galilee, as <hi type="italic">he said unto you,</hi> <reference osisRef="Matt.26.32">Matt. xxvi. 32</reference>. In their journey down into Galilee they would have time to recollect themselves, and call to mind what he had often said to them there, that he should suffer and die, and <hi type="italic">the third day be raised again;</hi> whereas while they were at Jerusalem, among strangers and enemies, they could not recover themselves from the fright they had been in, nor compose themselves to the due entertainment of better tidings. Note, [1.] All the meetings between Christ and his disciples are of his own appointing. [2.] Christ never forgets his appointment, but will be sure to meet his people with the promised blessing in every place where he records his name. [3.] In all meetings between Christ and his disciples, he is the most forward. <hi type="italic">He goes before you.</hi> <div eID="gen25063" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25064" type="x-p"/> IV. The account which the women did bring of this to the disciples (<reference osisRef="Mark.16.8">v. 8</reference>); They <hi type="italic">went out quickly,</hi> and <hi type="italic">ran from the sepulchre,</hi> to make all the haste they could to the disciples, <hi type="italic">trembling</hi> and <hi type="italic">amazed.</hi> See how much we are enemies to ourselves and our own comfort, in not considering and mixing faith with that Christ hath said to us. Christ had often told them, that <hi type="italic">the third day he would rise again;</hi> had they given that its due notice and credit, they would have come to the sepulchre, expecting to have found him risen, and would have received the news of it with a joyful assurance, and not with all this terror and amazement. But, being ordered to tell the disciples, because they were to tell it to all the world, they would not tell it to any one else, they showed not any thing of it to any man that they <hi type="italic">met by the way,</hi> for <hi type="italic">they were afraid,</hi> afraid it was too good news to be true. Note, Our disquieting fears often hinder us from doing that service to Christ and to the souls of men, which if faith and the <hi type="italic">joy of faith</hi> were strong, we might do.
entries.6fb583aeae35131334e0ff29c70984eac4e974f7: <div eID="gen25064" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s3">Christ's Appearances to Mary Magdalene and the Two Disciples.</title> <div sID="gen25065" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">9</hi> Now when <hi type="italic">Jesus</hi> was risen early the first <hi type="italic">day</hi> of the week, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, out of whom he had cast seven devils. <hi type="super">10</hi> <hi type="italic">And</hi> she went and told them that had been with him, as they mourned and wept. 11 And they, when they had heard that he was alive, and had been seen of her, believed not. <hi type="super">12</hi> After that he appeared in another form unto two of them, as they walked, and went into the country. <hi type="super">13</hi> And they went and told <hi type="italic">it</hi> unto the residue: neither believed they them. <div eID="gen25065" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25066" type="x-p"/> We have here a very short account of two of Christ's appearances, and the little credit which the report of them gained with the disciples. <div eID="gen25066" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25067" type="x-p"/> I. He appeared to Mary Magdalene, to her first in the garden, which we have a particular narrative of, <reference osisRef="John.20.14">John xx. 14</reference>. It was she <hi type="italic">out of whom he had cast seven devils;</hi> much was forgiven her, and much was given her, and done for her, and she <hi type="italic">loved much;</hi> and this honour Christ did her, that she was the first that saw him after his resurrection. The closer we cleave to Christ, the sooner we may expect to see him, and the more to see of him. <div eID="gen25067" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25068" type="x-p"/> Now, 1. She brings notice of what she had seen, to the disciples; not only to the <hi type="italic">eleven,</hi> but to the rest that followed him, <hi type="italic">as they mourned and wept,</hi> <reference osisRef="Mark.16.10">v. 10</reference>. Now was the time of which Christ had told them, that they should <hi type="italic">mourn and lament,</hi> <reference osisRef="John.16.20">John xvi. 20</reference>. And it was an evidence of their great love to Christ, and the deep sense they had of their loss of him. But when their <hi type="italic">weeping</hi> had <hi type="italic">endured a night</hi> or two, comfort returned, as Christ has promised; <hi type="italic">I will see you again, and your heart shall rejoice.</hi> Better news cannot be brought to disciples in tears, than to tell them of Christ's resurrection. And we should study to be comforters to disciples that are mourners, by communicating to them our experiences, and what we have <hi type="italic">seen of Christ.</hi> <div eID="gen25068" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25069" type="x-p"/> 2. They could not give credit to the report she brought them. They heard that <hi type="italic">he was alive,</hi> and had been seen of her. The story was plausible enough, and yet <hi type="italic">they believed not.</hi> They would not say that she made the story herself, or designed to deceive them; but they fear that she is <hi type="italic">imposed upon,</hi> and that it was but a fancy that she <hi type="italic">saw him.</hi> Had they believed the <hi type="italic">frequent</hi> predictions of it from his own mouth, they would not have been now so incredulous of the report of it. <div eID="gen25069" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25070" type="x-p"/> II. He appeared to two of the disciples, <hi type="italic">as they went into the country,</hi> <reference osisRef="Mark.16.12">v. 12</reference>. This refers, no doubt, to that which is largely related (<reference osisRef="Luke.24.13">Luke xxiv. 13</reference>, &c.), of which passed between Christ and the two disciples <hi type="italic">going to Emmaus.</hi> He is here said to have appeared to them in <hi type="italic">another form,</hi> in another dress than what he usually wore, in the form of a <hi type="italic">traveller,</hi> as, in the garden, in such a dress, that Mary Magdalene took him for the gardener; but that he had really his own countenance, appears by this, that <hi type="italic">their eyes were holden, that they should not know him;</hi> and when that restrain on <hi type="italic">their</hi> eyes was taken off, immediately they <hi type="italic">knew him,</hi> <reference osisRef="Luke.24.16-Luke.24.31">Luke xxiv. 16-31</reference>. Now, <div eID="gen25070" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25071" type="x-p"/> 1. These <hi type="italic">two</hi> witnesses gave in their <hi type="italic">testimony</hi> to this proof of Christ's resurrection; <hi type="italic">They went and told it to the residue,</hi> <reference osisRef="Mark.16.13">v. 13</reference>. Being <hi type="italic">satisfied</hi> themselves, they were desirous to give their brethren the <hi type="italic">satisfaction</hi> they had, that they might be comforted as they were. <div eID="gen25071" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25072" type="x-p"/> 2. This did not gain credit with all; <hi type="italic">Neither believed they them.</hi> They suspected that their eyes also deceived them. Now there was a wise providence in it, the proofs of Christ's resurrection were given in thus <hi type="italic">gradually,</hi> and admitted thus <hi type="italic">cautiously,</hi> that so the assurance with which the apostles preached this doctrine afterward, when they ventured their all upon it, might be the more satisfying. We have the more reason to believe those who did themselves believe so slowly: had they swallowed it presently, they might have been thought <hi type="italic">credulous,</hi> and their testimony the less to be <hi type="italic">regarded;</hi> but their <hi type="italic">disbelieving</hi> at first, shows that they did not believe it afterward but upon a full conviction.
entries.12c2136459e38373b4e5f61e90a4b36d3ff1de1b: <div eID="gen25072" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s3">Christ's Appearance to the Eleven.</title> <div sID="gen25073" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">14</hi> Afterward he appeared unto the eleven as they sat at meat, and upbraided them with their unbelief and hardness of heart, because they believed not them which had seen him after he was risen. <hi type="super">15</hi> And he said unto them, Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel to every creature. <hi type="super">16</hi> He that believeth and is baptized shall be saved; but he that believeth not shall be damned. <hi type="super">17</hi> And these signs shall follow them that believe; In my name shall they cast out devils; they shall speak with new tongues; <hi type="super">18</hi> They shall take up serpents; and if they drink any deadly thing, it shall not hurt them; they shall lay hands on the sick, and they shall recover. <div eID="gen25073" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25074" type="x-p"/> Here is, I. The <hi type="italic">conviction</hi> which Christ gave his apostles of the truth of his resurrection (<reference osisRef="Mark.16.14">v. 14</reference>); He <hi type="italic">appeared to them</hi> himself, when they were all together, <hi type="italic">as they sat at meat,</hi> which gave him an opportunity to <hi type="italic">eat and drink with them,</hi> for their full satisfaction; see <reference osisRef="Acts.10.41">Acts x. 41</reference>. And still, when he appeared to them, he <hi type="italic">upbraided them with their unbelief and hardness of heart,</hi> for even at the general meeting in <hi type="italic">Galilee, some doubted,</hi> as we find <reference osisRef="Matt.28.17">Matt. xxviii. 17</reference>. Note, The evidences of the truth of the gospel are so full, that those who receive it not, may justly be <hi type="italic">upbraided</hi> with their unbelief; and it is owing not to any weakness or deficiency in the proofs, but to the <hi type="italic">hardness of their heart,</hi> its senselessness and stupidity. Though they had not till now seen him themselves, they are justly blamed <hi type="italic">because they believed not them who had seen him after he was risen;</hi> and perhaps it was owing in part to the <hi type="italic">pride of their hearts,</hi> that they did not; for they thought, "If indeed he be risen, to <hi type="italic">whom should he delight to do</hi> the <hi type="italic">honour</hi> of showing himself but to us?" And if he <hi type="italic">pass them by,</hi> and show himself to <hi type="italic">others</hi> first, they cannot believe it is he. Thus many disbelieve the doctrine of Christ, because they think it <hi type="italic">below them</hi> to give credit to such as he had chosen to be the witnesses and publishers of it. Observe, It will not suffice for an excuse of our infidelity in the great day, to say, "<hi type="italic">We did not see him</hi> after he was risen," for we ought to have believed the testimony of those who did see him. <div eID="gen25074" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25075" type="x-p"/> II. The <hi type="italic">commission</hi> which he gave them to set up his kingdom among men by the preaching of his <hi type="italic">gospel,</hi> the glad tidings of reconciliation to God through a Mediator. Now observe, <div eID="gen25075" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25076" type="x-p"/> 1. <hi type="italic">To whom</hi> they were to preach <hi type="italic">the gospel.</hi> Hitherto they had been sent only to <hi type="italic">the lost sheep of the house of Israel,</hi> and were forbidden to go into the <hi type="italic">way of the Gentiles,</hi> or into any city of the Samaritans; but now their commission is enlarged, and they are authorized to <hi type="italic">go into all the world,</hi> into all parts of the world, the habitable world, and to <hi type="italic">preach the gospel</hi> of Christ to <hi type="italic">every creature,</hi> to the Gentiles as well as to the Jews; to every human creature that is capable of receiving it. "Inform them concerning Christ, the history of <hi type="italic">his life,</hi> and <hi type="italic">death,</hi> and <hi type="italic">resurrection;</hi> instruct them in the <hi type="italic">meaning</hi> and <hi type="italic">intention</hi> of these, and of the advantages which the children of men have, or may have, hereby; and invite them, without exception, to come and share in them. This is <hi type="italic">gospel.</hi> Let this be <hi type="italic">preached</hi> in all places, to all persons." These eleven men could not themselves preach it to all the world, much less to <hi type="italic">every creature</hi> in it; but they and the other disciples, seventy in number, with those who should afterward to be added to them, must <hi type="italic">disperse</hi> themselves several ways, and, wherever they went, carry the gospel along with them. They must send <hi type="italic">others</hi> to those places whither they could not <hi type="italic">go themselves,</hi> and, in short, make it the business of their lives to send those glad tidings <hi type="italic">up and down the world</hi> with all possible fidelity and care, not as an amusement or entertainment, but as a solemn message from God to men, and an appointed means of making men happy. "Tell as many as you can, and bid them tell others; it is a message of universal concern, and <hi type="italic">therefore,</hi> ought to <hi type="italic">have</hi> a universal welcome, because it <hi type="italic">gives</hi> a universal welcome." <div eID="gen25076" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25077" type="x-p"/> 2. What is the <hi type="italic">summary of the gospel</hi> they are to preach (<reference osisRef="Mark.16.16">v. 16</reference>); "Set before the world life and death, good and evil. Tell the children of men that they are all in a state of misery and danger, <hi type="italic">condemned</hi> by their prince, and <hi type="italic">conquered</hi> and <hi type="italic">enslaved</hi> by their enemies." This is supposed in their being <hi type="italic">saved,</hi> which they would not need to be if they were not <hi type="italic">lost.</hi> "Now go and tell them," (1.) "That if they <hi type="italic">believe the gospel,</hi> and give up themselves to be Christ's disciples; if they <hi type="italic">renounce</hi> the devil, the world, and the flesh, and be <hi type="italic">devoted</hi> to Christ as their prophet, priest, and king, and to God in Christ a their God in covenant, and evidence by their constant adherence to this covenant their sincerity herein, they <hi type="italic">shall be saved</hi> from the guilt and power of sin, it shall not <hi type="italic">rule</hi> them, it shall not <hi type="italic">ruin</hi> them. He that is a true Christian, shall be saved through Christ." <hi type="italic">Baptism</hi> was appointed to be the <hi type="italic">inaugurating</hi> rite, by which those that embraced Christ owned him; but it is here put rather for the <hi type="italic">thing signified</hi> than for the sign, for Simon Magus <hi type="italic">believed</hi> and was <hi type="italic">baptized,</hi> yet was not <hi type="italic">saved,</hi> <reference osisRef="Acts.8.13">Acts viii. 13</reference>. <hi type="italic">Believing with the heart, and confessing with the mouth the Lord Jesus</hi> (<reference osisRef="Rom.10.9">Rom. x. 9</reference>), seems to be much the same with this here. Or thus, We must <hi type="italic">as</hi>sent to gospel-truths, and <hi type="italic">con</hi>sent to gospel-terms. (2.) "<hi type="italic">If they believe not,</hi> if they receive not the record God gives concerning his Son, they cannot expect any other way of salvation, but must inevitably perish; <hi type="italic">they shall be damned,</hi> by the sentence of a <hi type="italic">despised</hi> gospel, added to that of a broken law." And even this is <hi type="italic">gospel,</hi> it is good news, that nothing else but unbelief shall damn men, which is a sin against the remedy. Dr. Whitby here observes, that they who hence infer "that the infant seed of believers are not capable of baptism, because they cannot believe, must hence also infer that they cannot be saved; <hi type="italic">faith</hi> being here more expressly required to salvation than to baptism. And that in the latter clause baptism is omitted, because it is not simply the want of baptism, but the contemptuous neglect of it, which makes men guilty of damnation, otherwise infants might be damned for the mistakes or profaneness of their parents." <div eID="gen25077" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25078" type="x-p"/> 3. What power they should be endowed with, for the confirmation of the doctrine they were to preach (<reference osisRef="Mark.16.17">v. 17</reference>); <hi type="italic">These signs shall follow them that believe.</hi> Not that all who believe, shall be able to produce these signs, but some, even as many as were employed in propagating the faith, and bringing others to it; for signs are intended <hi type="italic">for them that believe not;</hi> see <reference osisRef="1Cor.14.22">1 Cor. xiv. 22</reference>. It added much to the glory and evidence of the gospel, that the preachers not only wrought miracles themselves, but conferred upon others a power to work miracles, which power <hi type="italic">followed</hi> some of them that believed, wherever they went to preach. They shall do wonders <hi type="italic">in Christ's name,</hi> the same name into which they were baptized, in the virtue of power derived from him, and fetched in by prayer. Some particular signs are mentioned; (1.) They shall <hi type="italic">cast out devils;</hi> this power was more common among Christians than any other, and lasted longer, as appears by the testimonies of Justin Martyr, Origen, Irenæus, Tertullian Minutius Felix, and others, cited by Grotius on this place. (2.) They shall <hi type="italic">speak with new tongues,</hi> which they had never learned, or been acquainted with; and this was both a <hi type="italic">miracle</hi> (a miracle <hi type="italic">upon the mind</hi>), for the confirming of the truth of the gospel, and a <hi type="italic">means</hi> of spreading the gospel among those nations that had not heard it. It saved the preachers a vast labour in learning the languages; and, no doubt, they who by <hi type="italic">miracle</hi> were made <hi type="italic">masters of languages,</hi> were <hi type="italic">complete</hi> masters of them and of all their native elegancies, which were proper both to <hi type="italic">instruct</hi> and <hi type="italic">affect,</hi> which would very much recommend them and their preaching. (3.) They shall <hi type="italic">take up serpents.</hi> This was fulfilled in Paul, who was not hurt by the <hi type="italic">viper</hi> that <hi type="italic">fastened on his hand,</hi> which was acknowledged a great miracle by the barbarous people, <reference osisRef="Acts.28.5-Acts.28.6">Acts xxviii. 5, 6</reference>. They shall be kept unhurt by that <hi type="italic">generation of vipers</hi> among whom they live, and by the malice of the <hi type="italic">old serpent.</hi> (4.) If they be compelled by their persecutors to <hi type="italic">drink any deadly</hi> poisonous thing, <hi type="italic">it shall not hurt them:</hi> of which very thing some instances are found in ecclesiastical history. (5.) They shall not only be preserved from hurt themselves, but they shall be enabled to do good to others; <hi type="italic">They shall lay hands on the sick, and they shall recover,</hi> as multitudes had done by their master's <hi type="italic">healing</hi> touch. Many of the elders of the church had this power, as appears by <reference osisRef="Jas.5.14">Jam. v. 14</reference>, where, as an instituted sign of this miraculous healing, they are said to <hi type="italic">anoint</hi> the sick <hi type="italic">with oil in the name of the Lord.</hi> With what assurance of success might they go about executing their commission, when they had such credentials as these to produce!
entries.8ba6b6710a3a07c30258d6dfd17a59d28ba57fa2: <div eID="gen25078" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s3">The Ascension.</title> <div sID="gen25079" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">19</hi> So then after the Lord had spoken unto them, he was received up into heaven, and sat on the right hand of God. 20 And they went forth, and preached every where, the Lord working with <hi type="italic">them,</hi> and confirming the word with signs following. Amen. <div eID="gen25079" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25080" type="x-p"/> Here is, 1. Christ <hi type="italic">welcomed</hi> into the <hi type="italic">upper world</hi> (<reference osisRef="Mark.16.19">v. 19</reference>): <hi type="italic">After the Lord had spoken</hi> what he had to say to his disciples, he <hi type="italic">went up into heaven,</hi> in a cloud; which we have a particular account of (<reference osisRef="Acts.1.9">Acts i. 9</reference>), and he had not only an admission, but an abundant <hi type="italic">entrance,</hi> into his kingdom there; he was <hi type="italic">received up,</hi> received in state, with loud acclamations of the heavenly hosts; and he <hi type="italic">sat on the right hand of God:</hi> sitting in a posture of <hi type="italic">rest,</hi> for now he had finished his work, and a posture of <hi type="italic">rule,</hi> for now he took possession of his kingdom; he sat <hi type="italic">at the right hand of God,</hi> which denotes the sovereign dignity he is advanced to, and the universal agency he is entrusted with. Whatever God does concerning us, gives to us, or accepts from us, it is <hi type="italic">by his Son.</hi> Now he is glorified with the glory he had before the world. <div eID="gen25080" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25081" type="x-p"/> 2. Christ <hi type="italic">welcomed</hi> in this <hi type="italic">lower world;</hi> his being <hi type="italic">believed on in the world,</hi> and <hi type="italic">received up into glory,</hi> are put together, <reference osisRef="1Tim.3.16">1 Tim. iii. 16</reference>. (1.) We have here the apostles working diligently for him; they <hi type="italic">went forth, and preached every where</hi> far and near. Though the doctrine they preached, was <hi type="italic">spiritual</hi> and <hi type="italic">heavenly,</hi> and directly contrary to the <hi type="italic">spirit</hi> and <hi type="italic">genius</hi> of the world, though it met with abundance of opposition, and was utterly destitute of all secular supports and advantages, yet the preachers of it were neither <hi type="italic">afraid</hi> nor <hi type="italic">ashamed;</hi> they were so industrious in spreading the gospel, that within a few years the sound of it <hi type="italic">went forth into the ends of the earth,</hi> <reference osisRef="Rom.10.18">Rom. x. 18</reference>. (2.) We have here God <hi type="italic">working</hi> effectually <hi type="italic">with them,</hi> to make their labours successful, by <hi type="italic">confirming the word with signs following,</hi> partly by the miracles that were wrought upon the <hi type="italic">bodies</hi> of the people, which were divine seals to the Christian doctrine, and partly by the influence it had upon the <hi type="italic">minds</hi> of the people, through the operation of the Spirit of God, see <reference osisRef="Heb.2.4">Heb. ii. 4</reference>. These were properly <hi type="italic">signs following</hi> the word—the reformation of the world, the destruction of idolatry, the conversion of sinners, the comfort of saints; and these signs still follow it, and that they may do so more and more, for the honour of Christ and the good of mankind, the evangelist prays, and teaches us to say <hi type="italic">Amen.</hi> Father in heaven, thus let thy name be hallowed, and let thy kingdom come.  <chapter eID="Mark.16"/> <div eID="gen25081" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen24289" osisID="Mark" type="book"/>

entries.f20dfee00ff0ca3581c11241e2fd6e8adfc9a301: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv14191"/><title type="x-s2">CHAPTER 16</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Mark.16.1-Mark.16.20">Mr 16:1-20</reference>. Angelic Announcement to the Women on the First Day of the Week, that Christ Is Risen--His Appearances after His Resurrection--His Ascension--Triumphant Proclamation of His Gospel. ( = <reference osisRef="Matt.28.1-Matt.10.16">Mt 28:1-10, 16</reference>-20; <reference osisRef="Luke.24.1-Luke.24.51">Lu 24:1-51</reference>; <reference osisRef="John.20.1">Joh 20:1</reference>, 2, 11-29).</title> <div sID="gen27486" type="x-p"/> The Resurrection Announced to the Women (<reference osisRef="Mark.16.1-Mark.16.8">Mr 16:1-8</reference>).<div eID="gen27486" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen27487" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv14191"/><hi type="bold">1. And when the sabbath was past--</hi>that is, at sunset of our Saturday.<div eID="gen27487" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen27488" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Mary Magdalene--</hi>(See on <reference osisRef="Luke.8.2">Lu 8:2</reference>).<div eID="gen27488" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen27489" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">and Mary the mother of James--</hi>James the Less (see <reference osisRef="Mark.15.40">Mr 15:40</reference>).<div eID="gen27489" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen27490" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">and Salome--</hi>the mother of Zebedee's sons (compare <reference osisRef="Mark.15.40">Mr 15:40</reference> with <reference osisRef="Matt.27.56">Mt 27:56</reference>).<div eID="gen27490" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen27491" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">had bought sweet spices, that they might come and anoint him--</hi>The word is simply "bought." But our translators are perhaps right in rendering it here "had bought," since it would appear, from <reference osisRef="Luke.23.56">Lu 23:56</reference>, that they had purchased them immediately after the Crucifixion, on the Friday evening, during the short interval that remained to them before sunset, when the sabbath rest began; and that they had only deferred using them to anoint the body till the sabbath rest should be over. On this "anointing," see on <reference osisRef="John.19.40">Joh 19:40</reference>. <div eID="gen27491" type="x-p"/>
entries.93e6828cecd7189e2da9f543cd685ca3956b0cf4: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv14192"/><div sID="gen27492" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv14192"/><hi type="bold">2. And very early in the morning--</hi>(See on <reference osisRef="Matt.28.1">Mt 28:1</reference>).<div eID="gen27492" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen27493" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the first day of the week, they came unto the sepulchre at the rising of the sun--</hi>not quite literally, but "at earliest dawn"; according to a way of speaking not uncommon, and occurring sometimes in the Old Testament. Thus our Lord rose on the third day; having lain in the grave part of Friday, the whole of Saturday, and part of the following First day. <div eID="gen27493" type="x-p"/>
entries.3a5fe93cfcd16a51ecfe9d94e5413e516957266d: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv14193"/><div sID="gen27494" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv14193"/><hi type="bold">3. And they said among themselves--</hi>as they were approaching the sacred spot.<div eID="gen27494" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen27495" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Who shall roll us away the stone from the door of the sepulchre? ... for it was very great--</hi>On reaching it they find their difficulty gone--the stone already rolled away by an unseen hand. And are there no others who, when advancing to duty in the face of appalling difficulties, find their stone also rolled away? <div eID="gen27495" type="x-p"/>
entries.59b6456247552ab63b5713c864a1049edfbcee21: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv14194"/><div sID="gen27496" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv14194"/><hi type="bold">5. And entering into the sepulchre, they saw a young man--</hi>In <reference osisRef="Matt.28.2">Mt 28:2</reference> he is called "the angel of the Lord"; but here he is described as he appeared to the eye, in the bloom of a life that knows no decay. In Matthew he is represented as sitting on the stone outside the sepulchre; but since even there he says, "Come, see the place where the Lord lay" (<reference osisRef="Matt.28.6">Mt 28:6</reference>), he seems, as Alford says, to have gone in with them from without; only awaiting their arrival to accompany them into the hallowed spot, and instruct them about it.<div eID="gen27496" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen27497" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">sitting on the right side--</hi>having respect to the position in which His Lord had lain there. This trait is peculiar to Mark; but compare <reference osisRef="Luke.1.11">Lu 1:11</reference>.<div eID="gen27497" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen27498" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">clothed in a long white garment--</hi>On its length, see <reference osisRef="Isa.6.1">Is 6:1</reference>; and on its whiteness, see on <reference osisRef="Matt.28.3">Mt 28:3</reference>.<div eID="gen27498" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen27499" type="x-p"/> and they were affrighted. <div eID="gen27499" type="x-p"/>
entries.65630331db7df7b077c54de73761a58faea2472c: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv14195"/><div sID="gen27500" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv14195"/><hi type="bold">6. And he saith unto them, Be not affrighted--</hi>a stronger word than "Fear not" in Matthew (<reference osisRef="Matt.28.5">Mt 28:5</reference>).<div eID="gen27500" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen27501" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Ye seek Jesus of Nazareth, which was crucified!--</hi>"the Nazarene, the Crucified."<div eID="gen27501" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen27502" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">he is risen; he is not here--</hi>(See on <reference osisRef="Luke.24.5">Lu 24:5</reference>, <reference osisRef="Luke.24.6">6</reference>).<div eID="gen27502" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen27503" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">behold the place where they laid him--</hi>(See on <reference osisRef="Matt.28.6">Mt 28:6</reference>). <div eID="gen27503" type="x-p"/>
entries.f40e37f4b21591c082e087ef08cf006f4f4be04c: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv14196"/><div sID="gen27504" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv14196"/><hi type="bold">7. But go your way, tell his disciples and Peter--</hi>This Second Gospel, being drawn up--as all the earliest tradition states--under the eye of Peter, or from materials chiefly furnished by him, there is something deeply affecting in the preservation of this little clause by Mark alone.<div eID="gen27504" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen27505" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">that he goeth before you into Galilee; there shall ye see him, as he said unto you--</hi>(See on <reference osisRef="Matt.28.7">Mt 28:7</reference>). <div eID="gen27505" type="x-p"/>
entries.6d8b5965fb68360ec9ba71cb908e1cd469fec815: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv14197"/><div sID="gen27506" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv14197"/><hi type="bold">8. And they went out quickly, and fled from the sepulchre: for they trembled and were amazed--</hi>"for tremor and amazement seized them."<div eID="gen27506" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen27507" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">neither said they anything to any man; for they were afraid--</hi>How intensely natural and simple is this!<div eID="gen27507" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen27508" type="x-p"/> Appearances of Jesus after His Resurrection (<reference osisRef="Mark.16.9-Mark.16.18">Mr 16:9-18</reference>). <div eID="gen27508" type="x-p"/>
entries.f4b1017ed15a31e6d031c4bbd96ab9d131cdab60: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv14198"/><div sID="gen27509" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv14198"/><hi type="bold">9. Now when Jesus was risen early the first day of the week, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, out of whom he had cast seven devils--</hi>There is some difficulty here, and different ways of removing it have been adopted. She had gone with the other women to the sepulchre (<reference osisRef="Mark.16.1">Mr 16:1</reference>), parting from them, perhaps, before their interview with the angel, and on finding Peter and John she had come with them back to the spot; and it was at this second visit, it would seem, that Jesus appeared to this Mary, as detailed in <reference osisRef="John.20.11-John.20.18">Joh 20:11-18</reference>. To a woman was this honor given to be the first that saw the risen Redeemer, and that woman was NOT his virgin-mother. <div eID="gen27509" type="x-p"/>
entries.3c33899107755f8d22ee562137ce7d9f3a960a6e: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv14199"/><div sID="gen27510" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv14199"/><hi type="bold">11. And they, when they had heard that he was alive, and had been seen of her, believed not--</hi>This, which is once and again repeated of them all, is most important in its bearing on their subsequent testimony to His resurrection at the risk of life itself. <div eID="gen27510" type="x-p"/>
entries.d11eaf24f094f2e01f84f85a92282390925d03e1: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv14200"/><div sID="gen27511" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv14200"/><hi type="bold">12. After that he appeared in another form--</hi>(compare <reference osisRef="Luke.24.16">Lu 24:16</reference>).<div eID="gen27511" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen27512" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">unto two of them as they walked, and went into the country--</hi>The reference here, of course, is to His manifestation to the two disciples going to Emmaus, so exquisitely told by the Third Evangelist (see on <reference osisRef="Luke.24.13">Lu 24:13</reference>, &c.). <div eID="gen27512" type="x-p"/>
entries.f07aa105f57ec2e75c7b3ead90346d4e668fec70: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv14201"/><div sID="gen27513" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv14201"/>13. And they went and told it unto the residue: neither believed they them, &c. <div eID="gen27513" type="x-p"/>
entries.90a1a1354b9aad2ed712603c85c7149cbc8ecc3d: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv14202"/><div sID="gen27514" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv14202"/><hi type="bold">15. And he said unto them, Go ye into all the world, and preach the Gospel to every creature--</hi>See on <reference osisRef="John.20.19-John.20.23">Joh 20:19-23</reference> and <reference osisRef="Luke.24.36-Luke.24.49">Lu 24:36-49</reference>. <div eID="gen27514" type="x-p"/>
entries.4c3aafeb7fa8ab4e980729a823f65fd42b9c5e66: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv14203"/><div sID="gen27515" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv14203"/><hi type="bold">16. He that believeth and is baptized--</hi>Baptism is here put for the external signature of the inner faith of the heart, just as "confessing with the mouth" is in <reference osisRef="Rom.10.10">Ro 10:10</reference>; and there also as here this outward manifestation, once mentioned as the proper fruit of faith, is not repeated in what follows (<reference osisRef="Rom.10.11">Ro 10:11</reference>).<div eID="gen27515" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen27516" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">shall be saved; but he that believeth not shall be damned--</hi>These awful issues of the reception or rejection of the Gospel, though often recorded in other connections, are given in this connection only by Mark. <div eID="gen27516" type="x-p"/>
entries.3245bdc37d37d48a315dba4ae8b6f07d3be14274: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv14204"/><div sID="gen27517" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv14204"/><hi type="bold">17-18. And these signs shall follow them that believe ... They shall take up serpents--</hi>These two verses also are peculiar to Mark.<div eID="gen27517" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen27518" type="x-p"/> The Ascension and Triumphant Proclamation of the Gospel Thereafter (<reference osisRef="Mark.16.19">Mr 16:19</reference>, <reference osisRef="Mark.16.20">20</reference>). <div eID="gen27518" type="x-p"/>
entries.2c7425a60ec8e610f8d09813159647620dc12676: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv14205"/><div sID="gen27519" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv14205"/><hi type="bold">19. So then after the Lord--</hi>an epithet applied to Jesus by this Evangelist only in <reference osisRef="Mark.16.19">Mr 16:19</reference>, <reference osisRef="Mark.16.20">20</reference>, when He comes to His glorious Ascension and its subsequent fruits. It is most frequent in Luke.<div eID="gen27519" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen27520" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">had spoken unto them, he was received up into heaven--</hi>See on <reference osisRef="Luke.24.50">Lu 24:50</reference>, <reference osisRef="Luke.24.51">51</reference>.<div eID="gen27520" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen27521" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">and sat on the right hand of God--</hi>This great truth is here only related as a fact in the Gospel history. In that exalted attitude He appeared to Stephen (<reference osisRef="Acts.7.55">Ac 7:55</reference>, <reference osisRef="Acts.7.56">56</reference>); and it is thereafter perpetually referred to as His proper condition in glory. <div eID="gen27521" type="x-p"/>
entries.99c56dd2a6b66b22d6d56c7ce7f6d4c83829443d: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv14206"/><div sID="gen27522" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv14206"/><hi type="bold">20. And they went forth, and preached everywhere, the Lord working with them, and confirming the word with signs following. Amen--</hi>We have in this closing verse a most important link of connection with the Acts of the Apostles, where He who directed all the movements of the infant Church is perpetually styled "The Lord"; thus illustrating His own promise for the rounding and building up of the Church, "Lo, I AM WITH You alway!" <chapter eID="Mark.16"/><div eID="gen27522" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen26635" osisID="Mark" type="book"/>

entries.13f1e30e13435242c3600e0250a37d3f14ca5f1b: <div eID="gen39697" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s">Introduction</title> <div sID="gen39698" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen39699" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen39699" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen39698" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen39700" type="x-p"/> Early in the morning after the Sabbath, the three Marys come to the sepulcher, bringing sweet spices to embalm the body, <reference osisRef="Mar.16.1-Mar.16.4">Mar 16:1-4</reference>. They see an angel who announces the resurrection of our Lord, <reference osisRef="Mar.16.5-Mar.16.8">Mar 16:5-8</reference>. Jesus appears to Mary Magdalene, who goes and tells the disciples, <reference osisRef="Mar.16.9-Mar.16.11">Mar 16:9-11</reference>. He appears also to the two disciples who were going into the country, who also tell it to the rest, <reference osisRef="Mar.16.12">Mar 16:12</reference>, <reference osisRef="Mar.16.13">Mar 16:13</reference>. Afterwards he appears unto the eleven, and commissions them to preach the Gospel to all mankind, <reference osisRef="Mar.16.14-Mar.16.16">Mar 16:14-16</reference>. And promises to endue them with power to work miracles, <reference osisRef="Mar.16.17">Mar 16:17</reference>, <reference osisRef="Mar.16.18">Mar 16:18</reference>. He is received up into heaven, <reference osisRef="Mar.16.19">Mar 16:19</reference>. And they go forth to preach and work miracles, <reference osisRef="Mar.16.20">Mar 16:20</reference>. <div eID="gen39700" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen39701" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">Verse 1</hi> <div eID="gen39701" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen39702" type="x-p"/> And anoint him - Rather, to embalm him. This is a proof that they had not properly understood what Christ had so frequently spoken, viz. that he would rise again the third day. And this inattention or unbelief of theirs is a proof of the truth of the resurrection.
entries.a74180b7985d78cb297e82201d06a8a0d9d3c115: <hi type="bold">Verse 2</hi> <div eID="gen39702" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen39703" type="x-p"/> Very early in the morning, - This was the time they left their own houses, and by the rising of the sun they got to the tomb. As the preceding day was the Sabbath, they could not, consistently with the observances of that day, approach the tomb. See the concluding notes at the end of John. <div eID="gen39703" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen39704" type="x-p"/> The following observations from Lightfoot will serve to illustrate this subject. "The distinction of the twilight among the rabbins was this: - "I. איילחא השחרא The hinde of the morning - the first appearance. R. Chaiia Rab, and R. Simeon ben Chalaphta, travelling together on a certain morning in the valley of Arbel, saw the hinde of the morning, that its light spread the sky. R. Chaiia said, Such shall be the redemption of Israel. First, it goes forward by degrees, and by little and little; but by how much the more it shall go forward, by so much the more it shall increase. It was at that time that Christ arose, namely, in the first morning, as may be gathered from the words of St. Matthew. And to this the title of the 22d Psalm seems to have respect - על איילת השחר. See also <reference osisRef="Rev.22.16">Rev 22:16</reference>, I am the bright and morning star. And now you may imagine the women went out of their houses towards the sepulchre. "II. משיכיר בי הכלת ללב When one may distinguish between purple color and white. From what time do they recite their phylacterical prayers in the morning? From that time that one may distinguish between purple color and white. R. Eliezer saith, Between purple color and green. Before this time was obscurum adhue caeptae lucis, the obscurity of the begun light, as Tacitus's expression is. "III. משיארו המזרח When the east begins to lighten. "IV. בנץ החמה Sunrise; from the hinde of the morning going forth, until the east begins to lighten; and from the time the east begins to lighten, until sunrise, etc. "According to these four parts of time, one might not improperly suit the four phrases of the evangelists. According to the first, Matthew's, Τῃ επιφωσκουσῃ, As it began to dawn. According to the second, John's, Πρωΐ σκοτιας ετι ουσης, Early in the morning when it was yet dark. To the third, Luke's, Ορθρου βαθεως, Very early in the morning. To the fourth, Mark's, Λιαν πρωΐ, Very early in the morning. And yet, Ανατειλαντος του ἡλιου, At the rising of the sun. For the women came twice to the sepulchre, as St. John teaches, by whom the other evangelists are to be explained; which being well considered, the reconciling them together is very easy."
entries.21b2faaf2fafeb4043041a74f084ad5dd6dc8cfe: <hi type="bold">Verse 4</hi> <div eID="gen39704" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen39705" type="x-p"/> For it was very great - This clause should be read immediately after the third verse, according to D, three copies of the Itala, Syriac, Hier., and Eusebius. "Who shall roll us away the stone from the door of the sepulchre? for it was very great. And when they looked, they saw that the stone was rolled away." They knew that the stone was too heavy for them to roll away; and, unless they got access to the body, they could not apply the aromatics which they had brought to finish the embalming.
entries.4a3bab39797d3a98d7b3e89043b1da8c4717ae5e: <hi type="bold">Verse 6</hi> <div eID="gen39705" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen39706" type="x-p"/> Jesus of Nazareth - The Jews had given this name to Christ by way of reproach, <reference osisRef="Mat.2.23">Mat 2:23</reference>; but as it was under this name that he was crucified, <reference osisRef="Joh.19.19">Joh 19:19</reference>, the angel here, and the apostles after, have given him the same name, <reference osisRef="Act.4.10">Act 4:10</reference>, etc. Names which the world, in derision, fixes all the followers of God, often become the general appellatives of religious bodies: thus Quakers, Puritans, Pietists, and Methodists, have in their respective times been the nicknames, given in derision by the world, to those who separated themselves from its corruptions. Our Lord, by continuing to bear the name of the Nazarene, teaches us not to be too nice or scrupulous in fixing our own appellation. No matter what the name may be, as long as it implies no particular evil, and serves sufficiently to mark us out. Let us be contented to bear it, and thus carry about with us the reproach of Christ; always taking care to keep our garments unspotted from the world.
entries.d1c00845f6ebf68c04444c8b08c1a9171815a6bd: <hi type="bold">Verse 7</hi> <div eID="gen39706" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen39707" type="x-p"/> Tell his disciples and Peter - Why is not Peter included among the disciples? For this plain reason, - he had forfeited his discipleship, and all right to the honor and privileges of an apostle, by denying his Lord and Master. However, he is now a penitent: - tell him that Jesus is risen from the dead, and is ready to heal his backsliding, and love him freely; so that, after being converted, he may strengthen his brethren.
entries.6e95d25ae057528627fd9f3a33715d7e8967d952: <hi type="bold">Verse 9</hi> <div eID="gen39707" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen39708" type="x-p"/> Now when Jesus was risen, etc. - This, to the conclusion of the Gospel, is wanting in the famous Codex Vaticanus, and has anciently been wanting in many others. See Wetstein and Griesbach. In the margin of the later Syriac version, there is a remarkable addition after this verse; it is as follows: - And they declared briefly all that was commanded, to them that were with Peter. Afterward Jesus himself published by them, from east to west, the holy and incorruptible preaching of eternal salvation. Amen. <div eID="gen39708" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen39709" type="x-p"/> Mary Magdalene - It seems likely that, after this woman had carried the news of Christ's resurrection to the disciples, she returned alone to the tomb; and that it was then that Christ appeared to her, <reference osisRef="Joh.20.1-Joh.20.12">Joh 20:1-12</reference>; and a little after he appeared to all the women together, <reference osisRef="Mat.28.9">Mat 28:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Luk.24.16">Luk 24:16</reference>.
entries.408fbb0c5bea1409fb3cb611fad3314036e16041: <hi type="bold">Verse 10</hi> <div eID="gen39709" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen39710" type="x-p"/> Them that had been with him - Not only the eleven disciples, but several others who had been the occasional companions of Christ and the apostles. <div eID="gen39710" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen39711" type="x-p"/> Mourned and wept - Because they had lost their Lord and Master, and had basely abandoned him in his extremity.
entries.17cea637c6c68156caca443739c231ec9c9c495c: <hi type="bold">Verse 12</hi> <div eID="gen39711" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen39712" type="x-p"/> He appeared - unto two of them - These were the two who were going to Emmaus. The whole account is given by Luke, 24:13-34, where see the notes. <div eID="gen39712" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen39713" type="x-p"/> Dr. Lightfoot's criticism upon this passage is worthy of notice. "That, in the verses immediately going before, the discourse is of the two disciples going to Emmaus, is without all controversy. And then how do these things consist with that relation in Luke, who saith, That they two, returning to Jerusalem, found the eleven gathered together, and they that were with them; who said, The Lord is risen indeed, and has appeared to Simon? <reference osisRef="Luk.24.34">Luk 24:34</reference>. The word λεγοντας, saying, evidently makes those to be the words των ενδεκα, of the eleven, and of those that were gathered together with them; which, when you read the versions, you would scarcely suspect. For when that word is rendered by the Syriac, cad amrin; by the Arabic, wehom yekolon; by the Vulgate, dicentes; by the Italian, dicendo; by the French, disans; by the English, saying; who, I pray, would take it in another sense, than that those two that returned from Emmaus said, The Lord is risen indeed, etc.? But in the original Greek, when it is the accusative case, it is plainly to be referred to the eleven disciples, and those that were together with them; as if they had discoursed among themselves of the appearance made to Peter, either before, or now in the very access of those two coming from Emmaus. And yet, says this our evangelist, that when those two had related the whole business, they gave no credit to them; so that, according to Luke, they believed Christ was risen, and had appeared to Simon, before they told their story; but, according to Mark, they believed it not, no, not when they had told it. The reconciling therefore of the evangelists is to be fetched thence, that those words pronounced by the eleven, Ὁτι ηγερθη ὁ Κυριος οντως, etc., The Lord is risen indeed, etc., do not manifest their absolute confession of the resurrection of Christ, but a conjectural reasoning of the sudden and unexpected return of Peter. I believe that Peter was going with Cleophas into Galilee, and that being moved with the words of Christ, told him by the women, Say to his disciples and Peter, I go before you into Galilee - think with yourself how doubtful Peter was, and how he fluctuated within himself after his threefold denial, and how he gasped to see the Lord again, if he were risen, and to cast himself an humble suppliant at his feet. When therefore he heard these things from the women, (and he had heard it indeed from Christ himself, while he was yet alive, that when he arose he would go before them into Galilee), and when the rest were very little moved with the report of his resurrection, nor as yet stirred from that place, he will try a journey into Galilee, and Alpheus with him; which, when it was well known to the rest, and they saw him return so soon and so unexpectedly - Certainly, say they, the Lord is risen, and hath appeared to Peter, otherwise he had not so soon come back again. And yet, when he and Cleophas open the whole matter, they do not yet believe even them."
entries.94c4e0be4a197b862fdf5799c230289cbaec5653: <hi type="bold">Verse 14</hi> <div eID="gen39713" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen39714" type="x-p"/> And upbraided them with their unbelief - Never were there a people so difficult to be persuaded of the truth of spiritual things as the disciples. It may be justly asserted, that people of so skeptical a turn of mind would never credit any thing till they had the fullest evidence of its truth. The unbelief of the disciples is a strong proof of the truth of the Gospel of God. See the addition at the end.
entries.6024519cdef8888cd71920861d30f175e69eabe6: <hi type="bold">Verse 15</hi> <div eID="gen39714" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen39715" type="x-p"/> Go ye into all the world - See on <reference osisRef="Mat.28.19">Mat 28:19</reference> (note). <div eID="gen39715" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen39716" type="x-p"/> And preach the Gospel to every creature - Proclaim the glad tidings - of Christ crucified; and raised from the dead - to all the creation, πασῃ τῃ κτισει - to the Gentile world; for in this sense בריות berioth, is often understood among the rabbins; because He, through the grace of God, hath tasted death for Every man, <reference osisRef="Heb.2.9">Heb 2:9</reference>. And on the rejection of the Gospel by the Jews, it was sent to the whole Gentile world.
entries.eeecfd8f261cf7e81c35a08f920d92285ec1c072: <hi type="bold">Verse 16</hi> <div eID="gen39716" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen39717" type="x-p"/> He that believeth - He that credits this Gospel as a revelation from God: and is baptized - takes upon him the profession of it, obliging himself to walk according to its precepts: he shall be saved - redeemed from sin here, and brought at last to the enjoyment of my eternal glory. But he that believeth not, shall be damned - because he rejects the only provision that could be effectual to his soul's salvation.
entries.b0e39a71acbdf90d69262197043aefada21c4305: <hi type="bold">Verse 17</hi> <div eID="gen39717" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen39718" type="x-p"/> These signs shall follow - Or rather, accompany; this is the proper import of the original word παρακολουθησει, from παρα with, and ακολουθεω, I follow. <div eID="gen39718" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen39719" type="x-p"/> Them that believe - The believers, as we express it; i.e. the apostles, and all those who in those primitive times were endued with miraculous powers, for the confirmation of the doctrines they preached. <div eID="gen39719" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen39720" type="x-p"/> In my name - That is, by the authority and influence of the almighty Jesus. <div eID="gen39720" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen39721" type="x-p"/> Cast out devils - Whose kingdom Jesus Christ was manifested to destroy. <div eID="gen39721" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen39722" type="x-p"/> Speak with new tongues - This was most literally fulfilled on the day of pentecost, Acts 2:4-19.
entries.166b6591453ad9ae64fb99d4d1a4b453a7f52209: <hi type="bold">Verse 18</hi> <div eID="gen39722" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen39723" type="x-p"/> Take up serpents - Several MSS. add εν ταις χερσιν, in their hands - shall be enabled to give, when such a proof may be serviceable to the cause of truth, this evidence of their being continually under the power and protection of God, and that all nature is subject to him. This also was literally fulfilled in the case of Paul, <reference osisRef="Act.28.5">Act 28:5</reference>. <div eID="gen39723" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen39724" type="x-p"/> If they drink any deadly thing - Θανασιμον (φαρμακον) being understood - if they should through mistake, or accident, drink any poisonous matter, their constant preserver will take care that it shall not injure them. See a similar promise, <reference osisRef="Isa.43.2">Isa 43:2</reference>. <div eID="gen39724" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen39725" type="x-p"/> They shall lay hands on the sick - And I will convey a healing power by their hands, so that the sick shall recover, and men shall see that these are sent and acknowledged by the Most High. Several instances of this kind are found in the Acts of the Apostles. <div eID="gen39725" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen39726" type="x-p"/> That the apostles of our Lord should not lose their lives by poison is most fully asserted in this verse, and there is neither record nor tradition to disprove this. But it is worthy of remark, that Mohammed, who styled himself The Apostle Of God, lost his life by poison; and had he been a true apostle of God, he could not have fallen by it. Al Kodai, Abul Feda, and Al Janabi, give the following account. <div eID="gen39726" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen39727" type="x-p"/> When Mohammed, in the seventh year of the Hejra, a.d. 628, had taken the city of Kheebar, from the Arab Jews, he took up his lodgings at the house of Hareth, the father of Marhab the Jewish general, who had been slain at the taking of the city by Alee, the son-in-law of Mohammed. Zeenab the daughter of Hareth, who was appointed to dress the prophet's dinner, to avenge the fall of her people, and the death of her brother, put poison in a roasted lamb which was provided for the occasion. Bashar, one of his companions, falling on too hastily, fell dead on the spot. Mohammed had only chewed one mouthful, but had not swallowed it: though, on perceiving that it was poisoned, he immediately spat it out, yet he had swallowed a sufficiency of the juice to lay the foundation of his death; though this did not take place till about three years after: but that it was the cause of his death then, his dying words related by Al Janabi, and others, sufficiently testify. When the mother of Bashar came to see him in his dying agonies, he thus addressed her: "O mother of Bashar, I now feel the veins of my heart bursting through the poison of that morsel which I ate with thy son at Kheebar." <div eID="gen39727" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen39728" type="x-p"/> Abul Feda, Ebnol Athir, and Ebn Phares say, that the prophet acknowledged on his death-bed, that the poison which he had taken at Kheebar had tormented him from that time until then, notwithstanding blisters were applied to his shoulders, and every thing done in the beginning to prevent its effects. Al Kodai and Al Janabi relate, that when Zeenab was questioned why she did this, she answered to this effect: "I said in my heart, If he be a king, we shall hereby be freed from his tyranny; and if he be a prophet, he will easily perceive it, and consequently receive no injury." To support his credit, he pretended that the lamb spoke to him, and said that it was infected with poison! See Elmakin, p. 8. It was therefore policy in him not to put Zeenab to death. It has pleased God that this fact should be acknowledged by the dying breath of this scourge of the earth; and that several of even the most partial Mohammedan historians should relate it! And, thus attested, it stands for the complete and everlasting refutation of his pretensions to the prophetic spirit and mission. Vide Specimen Hist. Arabum, a Pocockio, p. 189, 190. Le Coran traduit par Savary, vol. i; p. 135, and 212. See also, The Life of Mohammed by Prideaux, 93, 101.
entries.83186cf60ec3da7b345627dffcad5efdd58086f9: <hi type="bold">Verse 19</hi> <div eID="gen39728" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen39729" type="x-p"/> After the Lord had spoken - These things, and conversed with them for forty days, he was taken up into heaven, there to appear in the presence of God for us.
entries.5c934f9b0836c87ef3c64e205e65edd963a8b7f8: <hi type="bold">Verse 20</hi> <div eID="gen39729" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen39730" type="x-p"/> The Lord working with them - This co-operation was twofold, internal and external. Internal, illuminating their minds, convincing them of the truth, and establishing them in it. External, conveying their word to the souls that heard it, by the demonstration of the Holy Ghost; convincing them of sin, righteousness, and judgment; justifying them by his blood, and sanctifying them by his Spirit. Though miraculous powers are not now requisite, because the truth of the Gospel has been sufficiently confirmed, yet this co-operation of God is indispensably necessary, without which no man can be a successful preacher; and without which no soul can be saved. <div eID="gen39730" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen39731" type="x-p"/> With signs following - Επακολουθουντων σημειων, the accompanying signs: viz. those mentioned in the 17th and 18th verses, and those others just now spoken of, which still continue to be produced by the energy of God, accompanying the faithful preaching of his unadulterated word. <div eID="gen39731" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen39732" type="x-p"/> Amen - This is added here by many MSS. and versions; but is supposed not to have made a part of the text originally. Griesbach, Bengel, and others, leave it out. <div eID="gen39732" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen39733" type="x-p"/> St. Jerome mentions certain Greek copies, which have the following remarkable addition to <reference osisRef="Mar.16.14">Mar 16:14</reference>, after these words - and reproached them for their unbelief and hardness of heart, because they did not believe those who had seen him after he was raised up: Et illi satisfaciebant dicentes: seculum istud iniquitatis et incredulitatis substantia est, quae non sinit per immundos spiritus verem Dei apprehendi virtutem. Idcirco, jam nunc revela justitiam tuam. "And they confessed the charge, saying: This age is the substance of iniquity and unbelief, which, through the influence of impure spirits, does not permit the true influence of God to be apprehended. Therefore, even now, reveal thy righteousness." <div eID="gen39733" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen39734" type="x-p"/> There are various subscriptions to this book in the MSS. and versions; the principal are the following: "The holy Gospel according to Mark is ended written by him - in Egypt - in Rome - in the Latin tongue - directed by Peter the 10th-12th year after the ascension of Christ - preached in Alexandria, and all its coasts." Dr. Lardner supposes this Gospel to have been composed a.d. 64 or 65, and published before the end of the last mentioned year. See the Preface. <div eID="gen39734" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen39735" type="x-p"/> The Gospel according to Mark, if not an abridgment of the Gospel according to Matthew, contains a neat, perspicuous abridgment of the history of our Lord; and, taken in this point of view, is very satisfactory; and is the most proper of all the four Gospels to be put into the hands of young persons, in order to bring them to an acquaintance with the great facts of evangelical history. But as a substitute for the Gospel by Matthew, it should never be used. It is very likely that it was written originally for the use of the Gentiles, and probably for those of Rome. Of this, there seem to be several evidences in the work itself. Of the other Gospels it is not only a grand corroborating evidence, but contains many valuable hints for completing the history of our Lord, which have been omitted by the others; and thus, in the mouths of Four witnesses, all these glorious and interesting facts are established. <div eID="gen39735" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen39736" type="x-p"/> One thing may be observed, that this Gospel has suffered more by the carelessness and inaccuracy of transcribers than any of the others: and hence the various readings in the MSS. are much more numerous, in proportion, than in the other evangelists. Every thing of this description, which I judged to be of real importance, I have carefully noted. <div eID="gen39736" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen39737" type="x-p"/> Though the matter of St. Mark's work came from the inspiration of the Holy Spirit, yet the language seems to be entirely his own: it is very plain, simple, and unadorned; and sometimes appears to approach to a degree of rusticity or inelegance. Whoever reads the original must be struck with the very frequent, and often pleonastic, occurrence of ευθεως, immediately, and παλιν, again, and such like; but these detract nothing from the accuracy and fidelity of the work. The Hebraisms which abound in it may be naturally expected from a native of Palestine, writing in Greek. The Latinisms which frequently occur are accounted for on the ground of this Gospel being written for the Gentiles, and particularly for the Roman people: this, it must be confessed, is only theory, but it is a theory which stands supported by many arguments, and highly presumptive facts. However this may be, the Gospel according to Mark is a very important portion of Divine revelation, which God has preserved by a chain of providences, from the time of its promulgation until now; and for which no truly pious reader will hesitate to render due praise to that God whose work is ever perfect. Amen.  <chapter eID="Mark.16"/> <div eID="gen39737" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen39043" osisID="Mark" type="book"/>

entries.625804ad3d457246109bb104a8ce07b57e894c4a:
MARK Chapter 16

Verses 1-8. See this passage explained on Mt 28:1-8

Verse 1. Sweet spices. Aromatics. Substances used in embalming. The idea of sweetness is not, however, implied in the original, Many of the substances used for embalming were bitter; as, e.g., myrrh, and none of them perhaps could properly be called sweet. The word spices expresses all that there is in the original.

Anoint him. Embalm him. Or, apply these spices to his body to keep it from putrefaction. This is proof that they did not suppose he would rise again. And the fact that they did not expect he would rise gives more strength to the evidence for his resurrection.

(u) "And when the" Mt 28:1, Lk 24:1, Jn 20:1
entries.b051424e20ea089a30ac565824d098e9e14b6396: Verse 4. It was very great. These words belong to the third verse: "Who shall roll us away the stone from the door of the sepulchre? for," the evangelist adds, "it was very great."
entries.be8ffce6ffe95424b4430e05ccc2c26ac3845997: Verse 5. Sitting on the right side. As they entered. The sepulchre was large enough to admit persons to go into it; not unlike, in that respect, our vaults.
entries.934da349b43a34062e842a58495294550b4600e9: Verse 7. And Peter. It is remarkable that Peter is singled out for special notice. It was proof of the kindness and mercy of the Lord Jesus. Peter, just before the death of Jesus, had denied him. He had brought dishonour on his profession of attachment to him. He had been brought to see the crime, and to weep bitterly. It would have been right if the Lord Jesus had from that moment cast him off, and noticed him no more. But he loved him still. Having loved him once, he loved unto the end, Jn 13:1.
